subject: Strategy for 100% stacked bar chart with variable bar width ?

messages.author: 92a46c9449c605e2
messages.subject: Strategy for 100% stacked bar chart with variable bar width ?
parts:
Hi ... might anyone be able to suggest a strategy for this?

I have two categorical variables and one numeric variable.

I need to create a 100% stacked bar chart where the width of the
stacked bars are relatively proportional.

I suspect I would use geom_bar, but don't know how to set the stacking
to unity (i.e. 100%). I also suspect that I'll need to use faceting
with 'free' scales to accommodate the variable width ... and I'll need
to only use one bar per facet.

Any thoughts or suggestions would be appreciated.

Thanks very much,
Mauricio

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Strategy for 100% stacked bar chart with variable bar width ?
parts:
Do you mean a mosaic plot or spine plot? That sounds like what you're
describing. There's no built in way to do that at the moment, but you
can always work out the positions yourself and then plot them. I'm
working on a package (https://github.com/hadley/productplots) to do
this for a wide range of plots of this type, but it's not quite ready
yet.

Hadley
